{
  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "text": "Data‑artifact: The two XBRL concepts appear because Tesla’s filings switched taxonomy versions over time. Early 10‑K/10‑Q filings used the legacy us‑gaap:Revenues concept, while later filings adopted the newer us‑gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax concept after the SEC updated its taxonomy to reflect ASC 606.",
      "how_to_test": "SELECT fiscal_year, concept, COUNT(DISTINCT accession_number) AS filings, MIN(filed_date) AS first_filing, MAX(filed_date) AS last_filing
FROM edgar.revenue_facts
WHERE cik = 1318605
  AND concept IN ('Revenues','RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax')
GROUP BY fiscal_year, concept
ORDER BY fiscal_year, concept;"
    },
    {
      "text": "Data‑artifact: Duplicate reporting of the same period in amended filings causes both concepts to appear for Tesla. When a company files an amendment (e.g., 10‑K/A) it may re‑tag the same financial line with a different concept, resulting in two rows for the same fiscal period but different accession numbers.",
      "how_to_test": "SELECT r1.fiscal_year, r1.fiscal_period, r1.accession_number AS orig_acc, r2.accession_number AS amend_acc,
       r1.concept AS orig_concept, r2.concept AS amend_concept
FROM edgar.revenue_facts r1
JOIN edgar.revenue_facts r2
  ON r1.cik = r2.cik
 AND r1.fiscal_year = r2.fiscal_year
 AND r1.fiscal_period = r2.fiscal_period
 AND r1.accession_number <> r2.accession_number
WHERE r1.cik = 1318605
  AND r1.concept IN ('Revenues','RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax')
  AND r2.concept IN ('Revenues','RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax')
  AND r1.form_type LIKE '10-%'
  AND r2.form_type LIKE '10-%'
ORDER BY r1.fiscal_year, r1.fiscal_period;"
    },
    {
      "text": "Real‑world: Tesla adopted ASC 606 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers) in FY 2018, requiring a separate XBRL element for revenue from contracts with customers excluding assessed taxes. The legacy 'Revenues' concept continued to be used for total GAAP revenue, so both concepts coexist post‑adoption.",
      "how_to_test": "SELECT fiscal_year,
       SUM(CASE WHEN concept = 'Revenues' THEN value_usd END) AS total_rev,
       SUM(CASE WHEN concept = 'RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax' THEN value_usd END) AS contract_rev
FROM edgar.revenue_facts
WHERE cik = 1318605
  AND concept IN ('Revenues','RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax')
GROUP BY fiscal_year
HAVING total_rev IS NOT NULL AND contract_rev IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY fiscal_year;"
    },
    {
      "text": "Real‑world: Tesla reports both total revenue and a subset representing revenue from vehicle sales and services (core contracts) while excluding regulatory credits and leasing revenue. The 'RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax' concept captures the core contract revenue, whereas 'Revenues' includes all streams (including energy generation, storage, and services).",
      "how_to_test": "SELECT fiscal_year,
       SUM(CASE WHEN concept = 'Revenues' THEN value_usd END) AS total_rev,
       SUM(CASE WHEN concept = 'RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax' THEN value_usd END) AS core_contract_rev,
       (SUM(CASE WHEN concept = 'Revenues' THEN value_usd END) -
        SUM(CASE WHEN concept = 'RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax' THEN value_usd END)) AS other_rev
FROM edgar.revenue_facts
WHERE cik = 1318605
  AND concept IN ('Revenues','RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax')
GROUP BY fiscal_year
ORDER BY fiscal_year;"
    }
  ]
}
